Simulate closure-unit detection data with known truth

Source: R/sim_closure_unit_data.R
sim_closure_unit_data.Rd

Simulates single-season data for the closure-unit families, occ() and the nmix() variants. Each covariate recipe holds per-site covariates for the latent state and per-visit covariates for detection. data_train is the long frame mvgam() and jsdgam() take. y_array is the four-dimensional layout of pivot_detection_array(). truth holds every generative parameter for recovery checks.

Usage

sim_closure_unit_data(
  type = 1L,
  family = occ(),
  n_species = 1L,
  n_sites = 30L,
  n_visits = 4L,
  n_lv = 0L,
  K_max = 30L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

type

Integer in 1:2 selecting the covariate recipe. See Details.

family

A closure-unit family: occ() (the default), nmix() ("poisson_binomial"), nmix("royle_nichols") or nmix("poisson_poisson").

n_species

Integer number of species. Defaults to 1L.

n_sites

Integer number of closure units per species. Defaults to 30L.

n_visits

Integer number of visits to every closure unit. Defaults to 4L.

n_lv

Integer number of latent factors shared by the species' state intercepts. Defaults to 0L, independent species. Requires n_species > 1L. See Latent factors.

K_max

Integer cap on the latent abundance N of an nmix() family. Defaults to 30L.

seed

Optional integer seed. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

Value

A list of class c("mvgam_sim_closure_unit", "mvgam_sim"):

data_train

Long data.frame. Its columns are series (the species), site, time (the site, which identifies the closure unit in a single season), visit, y, the site and visit covariates, then cap: 1 for occ(), K_max for nmix().

data_test

NULL. Closure-unit data have no held-out times.

y_array

Integer array [n_species, n_sites, 1, n_visits] for pivot_detection_array().

family, type

The family and recipe.

n_species, n_sites, n_visits, n_lv

The simulation dimensions.

truth

The generative parameters. See Truth bundle.

Details

type = 1

State predictor b0 + b1 * env, with env ~ N(0, 1) per site. Detection predictor c0 + c1 * tod_c, with tod_c ~ U(-6, 6) per visit, a centred time of day.

type = 2

State predictor b0 + b1 * env + b2 * elev, with env and elev each N(0, 1) per site. Detection predictor c0 + c1 * tod_c + c2 * effort, with tod_c ~ U(-6, 6) and effort ~ U(0.5, 1.5) per visit.

Each predictor is on the scale of the family's own link. The state predictor takes the logit for occ() and the log for every nmix() variant, where it sets the Poisson abundance mean lambda. The detection predictor takes the logit for occ(), nmix("poisson_binomial") and nmix("royle_nichols"). It takes the log for nmix("poisson_poisson"), whose encounter rate rho is unbounded.

Each species draws an intercept from a normal with mean zero. Each covariate draws one community mean. Each species then draws its slope around that mean. The standard deviations are:

PredictorInterceptCommunity meanSpecies slope
occ() state0.751.50.5
nmix() state0.50.40.3
Detection0.50.20.15

The nmix() state scales keep lambda well below K_max. The detection scales keep detection away from 0 and 1 across the range of tod_c.

Latent factors

With n_lv > 0L, the state predictor of species k at site i gains sum_l Z[k, l] * lv[i, l]. The [n_species x n_lv] loadings Z are normal with standard deviation 0.7. The [n_sites x n_lv] factor scores lv are standard normal. truth$loadings and truth$lv return both for comparison with jsdgam() estimates and ordinate().

Truth bundle

psi (occ) or lambda (nmix)

[n_species x n_sites] matrix of occupancy probabilities or expected abundances.

z (occ) or N (nmix)

[n_species x n_sites] matrix of the realised latent states that predict(fit, type = "latent_state") estimates.

p

[n_species x n_sites x n_visits] array of the detection parameter that predict(fit, type = "detection") estimates: the detection probability, the per-individual probability r of nmix("royle_nichols") or the encounter rate rho of nmix("poisson_poisson").

state_coefs, detection_coefs

The intercept and slopes of each predictor. A named vector for one species, an [n_species x (1 + p)] matrix for several.

loadings, lv

Z and the factor scores, when n_lv > 0L.

See also

sim_mvgam() simulates state-space time series. sim_jsdgam() simulates site-by-species data without a detection process. The N-mixture article fits occupancy and N-mixture models to data of this layout.

Other simulation: sim_jsdgam(), sim_mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# Four species with two site and two visit covariates
simdat <- sim_closure_unit_data(
  family    = occ(),
  n_species = 4L,
  n_sites   = 50L,
  n_visits  = 4L,
  type      = 2L,
  seed      = 1L
)
head(simdat$data_train)
#>   visit site series time y cap        env       elev      tod_c    effort
#> 1     1    1   sp_1    1 1   1 -0.6264538  0.3981059 -2.7899015 1.1588776
#> 2     2    1   sp_1    1 0   1 -0.6264538  0.3981059  3.1436863 1.4643170
#> 3     3    1   sp_1    1 1   1 -0.6264538  0.3981059  2.0845468 1.0541771
#> 4     4    1   sp_1    1 1   1 -0.6264538  0.3981059 -0.1662107 1.3708056
#> 5     1    2   sp_1    2 0   1  0.1836433 -0.6120264 -3.3762566 0.6850700
#> 6     2    2   sp_1    2 0   1  0.1836433 -0.6120264  5.1949179 0.9425101
summary(simdat)
#> Simulated closure-unit dataset (sim_closure_unit_data type 2)
#>   Family       : occ
#>   Species      : 4
#>   Sites        : 50
#>   Visits/unit  : 4
#> 
#> True generative parameters
#>   psi range: [0.000, 1.000]
#>   Detection range: [0.039, 0.959]
